subject: The American Housing Corporation
source_quote: Projected MOIC (5gmal.comDEAL SNAPSHOТ Issuer The American Housing Corporation Ownership 1.75% Round Series A Instrument Series A Preferred (Priced) Allocation Co-Invest: $5,000,000 Valuation Cap $235,000,000 (pre-money) THE OPPORTUNITY Residential construction has not meaningfully benefited from industrial-scale productivity improvements, despite a persistent housing shortage and structurally high construction costs. AHC's thesis is that the path to scale is not "modular houses as a product," but a repeatable, software-orchestrated manufacturing + assembly system that can be deployed across geographies with predictable cost, timeline, and quality. AHC's approach is componentized (e.g., bathrooms/kitchens + panels) and built for factory repeatability; each module is designed to fit standard shipping containers for cost-efficient logistics and national deployment. That production line is married with a software layer (Alamo) as the "manufacturing OS." Alamo is intended to manage underwriting, site planning, factory production, and onsite assembly-creating a compounding operational dataset and tighter feedback loops than contractor-led construction. AHC is explicitly structuring the business so real estate capital can fund land + builds (PropCo) while the venture-backed OpCo captures high-margin manufacturing + system IP-aligning the capital stack with the growth bottleneck (production capacity) for efficient scaling. AHC is raising $50M to build out their first "Gigafactory" that will enable AHC to drive costs lower, expand margins, and scale production from dozens of units a year to over a thousand. The Series A round is fully subscribed and led by Contrary Ventures. Our participation in their Seed round and leading their last Bridge round gives our LPs exclusive access to allocation. WHY NOW Manufacturing inflection AHC has moved from concept to validated system quickly, and the binding constraint is now production capacity-not demand. Capital structure advantage The OpCo/PropCo model is designed to scale with real estate capital while preserving venture-style upside in the manufacturing + software layer. Execution velocity The team has shown unusually fast iteration and delivery cadence-de-risking "can they build" and shifting the question to "can they scale." TEAM Name Role Riley Meik CEO Background Experience from SpaceX Starship, as founder of Evolution Space, building vertically integrated solid rocket motors, and as founder of Zero where he built kits for net-zero homes. Founder of Form Developers and a partner at Cross Properties. Former founder/CTO (Tudu) - a modern material procurement platform - and has manufacturing automation experience from General Motors TECHNOLOGY & MOAT What's already true mail Standardized building system + factory production designed for repeatability and quality control. $230/sf build costs on their demo unit and a roadmap to driving costs lower to $180/sf and increasing margins from 15% to 30% Speed of manufacturing is several times faster than traditional stick-built; currently it takes 8 weeks to manufacture a 1800 sf townhouse and just 5 weeks to install and finish on site Alamo software layer is already in production and supporting the full lifecycle 5-YEAR RETURN SCENARIOS What compounds the moat mail Manufacturing learning curve: yield, automation, cycle-time compression, and procurement leverage as volume scales. Software-driven orchestration across underwriting → production planning → onsite assembly (data flywheel + operational switching costs as volume scales). Capital flywheel (OpCo/PropCo): real estate capital increases throughput; throughput improves unit economics; improved economics attracts more capital and expands markets.
